fact_sheet.business_description: The Company operates a travel-payments franchise connecting cardholders, merchants, and a service promise, while also engaging in financial-services activities [D01]. It is currently undergoing a strategic refocusing away from an unfocused financial conglomerate toward its core payments and financial-services franchises [D03].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Charge-card and payment services connecting cardholders and merchants, relying on customer confidence and merchant acceptance [D01, D03, D06].
economics: Travel payments combine service charges with funds held between receipt and settlement; fee income and balances are not free capital if obligations grow [D01, D06].
Pretax margins for segment activities: travel-related services (14.6%), investment/advisory (19.8%), and banking (17.3%) [D06].
Return on equity: travel-related services 23.8% (vs 12.2% prior), bank 10.03% (vs 11.97% prior) [D06].
earnings_record: Net income for 1989-1993: $1,157/$181/$789/$461/$1,478 million; 1993 continuing income included a $433 million gain [D02].
Q2 1994 continuing net income $359 million vs $301 million in Q2 1993 [D03].
competitive_position: Recognized travel-payments brand; competitive pressure exists in merchant charges, cardholder benefits, and funding costs [D01, D06].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Assets include customer settlement funding, which is not unencumbered industrial cash [D02, D04].
management_and_capital_allocation: Leadership is refocusing the company away from an unfocused financial conglomerate [D01, D03].
price_and_valuation: Historical normalized P/E: 11.52x based on $2.30 FY1993 adjusted continuing EPS [D04].

yields_pct.basis: Earnings yield calculated as $2.30 (FY1993 adjusted EPS) / $26.50 [D04]. Dividend yield based on $0.225 quarterly dividend [D04]. Treasury yield from FRED DGS10 [D04].

what_the_market_is_worried_about: Competitive card networks, merchant resistance to fees, consumer credit exposure, and the difficulty of reversing an unfocused conglomerate strategy [D05].
deal_terms_if_any: Existing $300 million 8.85% preferred investment originated in 1991; agreement calls for conversion after three years, subject to extension [D02].
recent_events: July 25, 1994: Release of Q2 1994 results showing 16.7% growth in continuing EPS [D03].
berkshire_context: Berkshire holds a $300 million preferred investment [D02].
Existing economic exposure noted; current decision concerns potential additional common ownership [D07, D08].
document_conflicts: Revenue figures differ between original presentation and later net-revenue presentations [D02].
missing_data: Complete current cash-flow and tangible-capital reconciliation; current-year full earnings guidance; dated external peer valuation grid [D03, D04, D06].

understandable.evidence: The company operates a core travel-payments franchise connecting cardholders and merchants, a business model that is long-standing and easy to understand [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: The company possesses a recognized travel-payments brand and a vast network of 3.7 million merchant locations, which creates a competitive advantage [D01, D03].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: While historical net income has fluctuated, the company has shown a rebound in continuing earnings, including 16.7% growth in Q2 1994, and is successfully shedding non-core conglomerate assets [D02, D03].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: The travel-related services segment demonstrates a strong 23.8% return on equity, and for financial institutions of this type, deposits and float are standard funding, not debt [D06].

capital_intensity.evidence: The business generates high returns on capital and, as a payments franchise, is not inherently capital-intensive in the manner of industrial manufacturing [D06].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Leadership is explicitly refocusing the company away from an unfocused conglomerate toward its core, value-creating payments franchise [D01, D03].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: With a market cap of approximately $13.12 billion, the company is sufficiently large to meaningfully impact Berkshire's portfolio [D04].

price_screen.evidence: The trailing earnings yield of 8.68% against a long bond yield of 7.13% represents a reasonable entry point for a quality franchise in this era [D04].

conflicts_resolved: Revenue figures differ between original presentation and later net-revenue presentations [D02] -> I relied on the adjusted continuing EPS and normalized earnings yield provided in D04 for valuation, as these are the primary metrics used to assess the core franchise's profitability.
gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a recognizable travel-payments franchise successfully returning to its core strengths with high returns on capital

gate2.why_available: The market remains skeptical due to the company's past struggles as an unfocused conglomerate and fears regarding competitive pressures in the payments industry [D05]. We believe the market under-rates the durability of the core travel-payments franchise, which is successfully shedding non-core assets to refocus on its high-ROE strengths [D01, D03, D06]. As management executes this refocusing, the earnings power of the core franchise will become increasingly apparent to the market [D03].
evidence: Q2 1994 continuing net income grew 16.7% compared to the prior year [D03].
The travel-related services segment currently maintains a 23.8% return on equity [D06].
The company has expanded its merchant network to 3.7 million locations [D03].
Strategic shift away from conglomerate structure is explicitly underway [D01, D03].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market fears that merchant resistance to fees and competitive card networks will permanently impair the company's ability to generate value, while remaining unconvinced by the turnaround efforts [D05].
what_must_be_true: The core travel-payments brand remains the primary utility for its cardholders and merchants despite competition.
Management continues to successfully divest non-core assets and reduce organizational complexity.
The travel-payments franchise maintains its pricing power despite merchant resistance to fees.

key_assumptions: Core travel-payments franchise retains pricing power [D06]
Successful divestiture of non-core conglomerate assets [D01]

gate3.price_vs_value: Price of $26.50 [D04] is roughly fair value; limited margin of safety at current market levels.
gate3.alternatives: Existing holdings or Berkshire buybacks are preferred as they offer more certainty than the current turnaround execution [D07, D08].
gate3.downside_case: Failure to successfully refocus the conglomerate results in continued margin compression from competitive card networks; permanent loss is unlikely given the underlying franchise value.
flagged_assumptions: Owner earnings estimated using reported continuing EPS as a proxy for maintenance capital requirements [D04]

gate4.role_description: permanent_passive_holder — value realised by the business compounding and rational capital allocation; Berkshire's edge is patience and permanent capital (default for marketable securities after 1980) [D07, D08]
value_realisation_path: the company's core travel-payments franchise continues to compound through its merchant network and cardholder utility [D01, D03, D06]
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In the 1980-1999 era, Berkshire prioritizes wonderful consumer franchises; as a non-controlling equity position, a passive holding role allows us to benefit from the turnaround without the risks of operational restructuring [D01, D03]

kill_criteria: Pricing power lost to competing card networks or merchant resistance to fee structures
Management fails to divest remaining non-core conglomerate assets
Significant deterioration in credit quality of the cardholder base
Capital adequacy ratios fall below regulatory requirements
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Must maintain sufficient liquidity for insurance obligations; must avoid concentrated positions that cannot be exited without impacting market price [D07, D08].
gate5.opportunity_cost: Capital is better deployed in existing holdings or Berkshire stock buybacks if available, as the company remains in a turnaround phase [D07, D08].
gate5.decider_reason: Buffett makes decisions on significant equity positions in recognizable consumer franchises within his circle of competence.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The turnaround execution fails to restore the franchise's historical pricing power and margins against growing competitive pressures.

valuation.owner_earnings: Normalised earnings approximated at $2.30 per share [D04]
valuation.downside_case: Failure to successfully refocus the conglomerate results in continued margin compression from competitive card networks; permanent loss is unlikely given the underlying franchise value.

drivers.driver: The stock trades at $26.50 against an estimated intrinsic value of $25.00 to $30.00, providing insufficient margin of safety [D04].
While the travel-payments franchise has a durable moat, the company is still in the midst of a turnaround from being an unfocused conglomerate [D01, D03].
Capital is better deployed in our existing holdings or Berkshire stock buybacks, which offer higher certainty than this turnaround execution [D07, D08].
The travel-related services segment demonstrates high returns on capital of 23.8%, yet the overall business remains burdened by organizational complexity [D06].

kill_criteria: Pricing power lost to competing card networks or merchant resistance to fee structures
Management fails to divest remaining non-core conglomerate assets
Significant deterioration in credit quality of the cardholder base
Capital adequacy ratios fall below regulatory requirements
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A significant reduction in price providing a wider margin of safety, or evidence that the divestiture of non-core assets is substantially complete and margin growth is accelerating.
final.memo:
The Company operates a core travel-payments franchise connecting cardholders and merchants, a business model that is long-standing and easy to understand [D01]. We have long admired the utility the brand provides to its 3.7 million merchant locations [D01, D03].

The travel-related services segment currently maintains a 23.8% return on equity, reflecting the significant power of the payments network [D06]. While competitive pressures exist, the core business remains a strong franchise [D01, D06].

Leadership is currently focused on divesting non-core conglomerate assets to return the business to its roots [D01, D03]. We trust management to execute this refocusing, though it is a process that takes time [D03].

Currently, the market values the company at $26.50, which is roughly fair value compared to our intrinsic value estimate of $25.00 to $30.00 [D04]. With only a limited margin of safety, we find the opportunity lacks the compelling upside we require [D04].

Capital is better deployed in existing holdings or Berkshire stock buybacks, where we see more certainty in the outcome [D07, D08]. We will continue to watch the execution of the turnaround, but we pass on initiating a new position at this price [D04, D08].
